identity.title: Unlocking the Power of Function Vectors for Characterizing and Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Instruction Tuning

problem.claim: The paper addresses catastrophic forgetting in LLMs during continual instruction tuning, where learning new tasks can impair previously learned information.

gap.claim: Prior work largely studies forgetting under a single training sequence, leaving the effects of diverse tasks and model differences insufficiently characterized.

contributions.claim: It uses function vectors as compact, model-dependent indicators for interpreting catastrophic forgetting in LLMs.
The authors report that forgetting primarily arises from biases in function activation rather than overwriting task-processing functions.
It proposes function-vector-guided training with regularization intended to stabilize function vectors and mitigate forgetting.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their function-vector-guided training methodology as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical and empirical analyses supporting the account that activation bias, rather than function overwriting, is the primary source of forgetting.
The authors report that tests on four benchmarks confirm the effectiveness of the proposed training method and support their theoretical framework.
Across varied settings, the authors report that forgetting depends on both the training tasks and the model.

narrative_sequence.summary: Catastrophic forgetting is introduced as the loss of previously learned information after new-task learning, including in LLM continual learning.
The paper identifies the single-sequence focus of much prior work and examines forgetting across varied tasks and settings.
Function vectors are presented as compact, model-dependent indicators for characterizing forgetting.
The authors attribute forgetting mainly to function-activation bias and derive a regularized, function-vector-guided training method.
Four-benchmark tests are reported to support the method and the proposed account of model-function dynamics.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects variation in forgetting across tasks and models to a model-dependent function-vector analysis, then links that analysis to a targeted regularizer.

lessons.interpretation: A useful research pattern is to align an explanatory representation with the mechanism targeted by an intervention.
lessons.application: For a continual-learning paper, define a task- and model-sensitive internal representation, state the hypothesized failure mechanism, and make the training constraint explicitly act on that representation.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the representation is not shown to track the target behavior or when internal representations cannot be measured reliably.

unknowns: The abstract does not name the four benchmarks, baselines, metrics, model families, task settings, or regularization details.
The reported confirmation does not specify effect sizes, statistical uncertainty, or the conditions under which the method may fail.
The abstract does not provide enough detail to assess the theoretical analyses or independently verify the stated novelty.
